quotes.quote: It is the only thing we expose to the internet.

rows.rationale: The source states it outright and states that nothing else is exposed, so the row is exclusive: a catalog that reads it may close the world on exposure.

The source says the order service is not exposed outside. model.json records the same value with an assumption calling it a statement of intent; an assertion says what the source states and nothing about the deployed system, so the basis is stated. Weakest reading in this file: the reviewer may prefer inferred.

quotes.quote: The order service is a Python worker in our core network

rows.rationale: The source places the order service in the core network, which the model's core-services zone stands for (case.json holds the alias).

assertion.subject: process:storefront-api
assertion.explanation: The storefront API is the only component the source exposes to the internet, and the model gives that tier its own zone.

rows.rationale: The source names no zone for the storefront API; the DMZ is the model's placement of the one internet-exposed component.

assertion.subject: store:orders-db
assertion.explanation: The order service reads and writes orders-db, and the source places the order service in the core network.

rows.rationale: The source never places the database; the order service, which is in the core network, reads and writes it.

assertion.subject: store:receipt-archive
assertion.explanation: The order service writes the receipt archive, and the source places the order service in the core network.

rows.rationale: The source never places the bucket; the order service writes it.

assertion.subject: entity:shopper
assertion.explanation: Shoppers reach the storefront API, which the source exposes to the internet and nothing else.

rows.rationale: Shoppers reach the storefront API, the one component exposed to the internet.

assertion.subject: entity:card-processor
assertion.explanation: The source calls the card processor a third party, and its webhook reaches the storefront API, the one internet-exposed component.

rows.rationale: A third party that calls back over the internet to the exposed component.

quotes.quote: Our card processor is a third party.

rows.rationale: The source states the processor is a third party, which is the one ownership fact in the text.

assertion.subject: flow:shopper-to-storefront-api:place-order
assertion.value: email and password sign-in issuing a session cookie

quotes.quote: Shoppers sign in with email and password and get a session cookie

rows.rationale: Stated mechanism on the shopper's interaction. The cookie is recorded on the principal below rather than as a second predicate here, so the projection into authentication stays a value.
What a signed-in shopper presents after sign-in.

quotes.quote: we have not rolled out MFA for shopper accounts yet

rows.rationale: An explicit absence, stated: the fact the assertion layer exists to keep.

quotes.quote: There is no auth on that gRPC call

rows.rationale: An explicit absence, stated. model.json reads it as 'none; accepted by network position'.

assertion.subject: anything that can reach the order service

quotes.quote: the order service accepts anything that can reach it

rows.rationale: The source states the whole check is reachability. 'Meant to be only the storefront API' is intent and is not a grant, so the principal is what the source names: anything that can reach it. The reviewer may prefer to name the storefront API.

assertion.subject: flow:order-service-to-orders-db:read-write-orders
assertion.value: a single application account with a password

quotes.quote: the order service reads and writes with a single application account

rows.rationale: Stated mechanism. The source says 'single'; whether the account is shared between principals is the disputed reading below.

quotes.quote: a single application account that has full read/write

rows.rationale: The grant the source states, with its resource and operation.

quotes.quote: The password comes from an environment variable on the worker.

rows.rationale: The source names the password as the credential the worker holds.

assertion.subject: application account password
assertion.value: an environment variable on the worker

quotes.quote: The password comes from an environment variable on the worker.

rows.rationale: Stated custody; registry version 2 added the predicate for this sentence.

assertion.subject: application account password
assertion.explanation: The source says the order service reads and writes with a single application account, so every instance and every operation presents one password.

rows.rationale: Inferred, not stated: one account serves every operation and every instance of the order service. The source says 'single', which is not 'shared'. model.json writes 'shared' into the attribute as if stated; see disputed.

quotes.quote: That is on TLS with the order service's own service account

rows.rationale: Stated transport protection.

assertion.subject: flow:order-service-to-receipt-archive:append-receipt
assertion.value: the order service's own service account

quotes.quote: That is on TLS with the order service's own service account

rows.rationale: Stated mechanism on the archive write.

quotes.quote: Every completed order also gets a receipt written to a Cloud Storage bucket

rows.rationale: The write the source states the order service performs.

quotes.quote: the bucket is encrypted with a customer-managed key

rows.rationale: Stated protection at rest.

quotes.quote: I would have to check how that callback is authenticated.

rows.rationale: The speaker raises the question and does not answer it: a hedged unknown, which a produced catalog must retain rather than fill.

disputed.proposed: keep HTTPS and record an assumption on this flow, or set unknown
disputed.basis: The source says 'That is on TLS' to a Cloud Storage bucket. TLS is stated and sits in encryption_in_transit; HTTPS is the transport a bucket write over TLS uses, which the source does not say. No assumption records the inference.

disputed.proposed: keep the value and record an assumption on this flow, or set unknown
disputed.basis: The source says the data lives in a PostgreSQL database that the order service reads and writes. The wire protocol follows from the product and is not stated. No assumption records the inference.

disputed.blessed: single shared application account with full read/write; password from an environment variable
disputed.proposed: single application account with full read/write; password from an environment variable
disputed.basis: The source says 'a single application account'. 'Shared' is the drafter's reading that one account serves every instance and operation; it is not the source's word, and corrections.md records it as one of the two facts that carry the threat. The catalog keeps it as an inferred credential-sharing row.
